headline: Experience isn't what happens to you—it's what you make of what happens
fun_facts: Research shows that people who regularly reflect on experiences learn up to twice as fast as those who don't
The ancient Stoics practiced daily reflection, reviewing each day's events each evening
Studies indicate that writing about experiences increases both learning and emotional processing
discussion_questions: What's a lesson from this year that you almost missed?
How do you currently reflect on your experiences?
What might you learn from an experience you haven't fully processed?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We learn more from experience than from anything else—but not automatically. Experience without reflection is just time passing. Today we explore how to extract wisdom from what you've already lived through.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Two people can go through the same experience and learn completely different amounts. The difference isn't intelligence—it's reflection. Why does reflection multiply learning?

options.text: It forces you to notice patterns
options.response: Exactly. Without reflection, events blur together. Reflection crystallizes lessons that would otherwise evaporate.
Time helps, but passive time doesn't teach. Active reflection is what extracts meaning from raw experience.

q1.title: The Reflection Gap
q1.script: Studies show that taking time to reflect after an experience can double retention and learning. But most people skip this step—they rush to the next thing. The gap between doing and learning is bridged by pausing to think.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Reflection Gap"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Right Questions
q2.script: Effective reflection isn't just remembering—it's questioning. What worked? What didn't? What would I do differently? What does this reveal about me? These questions transform raw experience into usable insight.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Written Reflection
q3.script: Writing deepens reflection. When you write about an experience, you're forced to structure your thoughts, notice gaps in understanding, and commit to interpretations. A journal isn't just storage—it's a thinking tool.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Your past is a library, not just a memory. But the books don't organize themselves. Take time to read your own story with curiosity. The lessons are there—you just have to look.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's today's lesson on reflective learning. Tomorrow, we'll explore marking what matters. Until then, take a moment to reflect on something from this year.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Year-End Reflection - The Learning Harvest
growTrack.learning_objective: Extract key lessons from the past year through structured reflection
growTrack.activity: Write down three significant experiences from this year. For each, answer: What happened? What did I feel? What did I learn? What would I do differently? Keep these insights somewhere you'll revisit.
